summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Thubten Chökyi Dorje and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nani Gopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1923). He served as Superintendent of the Indian Museum's Archæological Section (~1929–1938) and as Superintendent with the Archaeological Survey of India (1931).
Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Stony Brook University as a visiting scholar under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He served on Tohoku University's faculty (~1985–1993) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).
Naoki Kano (1868–1947) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895). He took up a post at Kyoto University in 1906 and taught Taichiro Kobayashi.
Naoki Nabeshima (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Tohoku University by 2002 under Toshifumi Goto. She worked at Tohoku University as a researcher (attested 2012) and later as a professor (attested 2026).

Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. A former British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University, she serves as Professor and Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (1974).
Naoya Funahashi (born 1947) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an encouragement researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at St. Benedict's College, Ceylon University College (~1921–1924), and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana (~1916–1955). He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya (~1955–1983).

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (born 1924) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD from the University of Delhi (1957–1961), where he was also a research fellow, and later served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1967, attested 1990 and 1999).

Nariaki Nakazato (born 1946) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and the University of Calcutta (PhD 1979–1985), he served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (1984–2010) and held posts at CEACS and Kobe University.
Narimoto Tamayama (born 1923) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).
Natalie Gummer is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1975) under Stephan Beyer. She also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman (born 1976) is a history and archaeology scholar who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and joined the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2005. She has held academic positions at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and the University of Virginia.
